verdict.rationale: AWS documents bulk operations across many resources through CloudFormation: one template provisions all described resources, and deleting a stack removes every resource in it. Resource Groups can organize resources by tag or stack, but the evidence never shows actions run against a group. CLI scripting is a user-built workaround, not a native bulk feature. missing for 10: native batch APIs for bulk item-level operations (e.g. bulk updates of data items or objects), documented bulk actions on tag-based resource groups, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: You create a template that describes all the AWS resources that you want (like Amazon EC2 instances or Amazon RDS DB instances), and CloudFormation takes care of provisioning and configuring those resources for you.
You can delete the stack just as easily, which deletes all the resources in the stack.
